subject: Urgent: multi-country remit lock — propose soft-dunning + legal hold
messages:
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Carlos Mendez <carlos@novumhealth.com>, accounts-payable@novumhealth.com
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 13 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0500
Subject: Outstanding invoice #INV-20261031 — VAT allocation and remit lock

Hi Carlos —

Following up on invoice INV-20261031 (total EUR 112,450) which is now 30 days past due. Our finance team logged a failed remit attempt on 11/01 (attached payment stub) and we received a note from your AP that the payment is being held pending clarification on VAT reverse-charge and entity routing.

To keep this from escalating:
- Can you confirm which NovumHealth entity is responsible for this invoice and provide the local VAT proof (reverse-charge acceptance or VAT ID)?
- If the VAT treatment is correct on your side, please share the bank payment reference or confirmation so we can release the remittance lock.

For transparency, because this is a multi-country invoicing scenario (invoice issued by Redwood EU Ltd.), we have temporarily put the account on a soft remit lock — this prevents new purchases and automatic renewals but does not suspend runtime. Our collections playbook calls for a soft-dunning sequence while we gather tax evidence.

Next steps I propose this week:
1) Novum provides VAT evidence or payment confirmation within 48 hours.
2) If we receive payment proof, we lift the remit lock and close the ticket.
3) If not, we will proceed with a formal dunning email and escalate to senior leadership / legal for contract review.

Attachments: NovumHealth_Invoice_20261031.pdf (PDF, 120KB), PaymentProof_Novum_20261101.png (PNG, 45KB)

Appreciate a quick reply — if helpful, happy to jump on a 15-min call to unblock.

Best,
Hannah
Hannah Schmitt
Senior Account Manager — Revenue Operations
Redwood Inference
[hannah_schmitt@redwood.com]

From: Carlos Mendez <carlos@novumhealth.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
Cc: Finance Controller <finance-controller@novumhealth.com>, accounts-payable@novumhealth.com
Date: Fri, 13 Nov 2026 11:04:00 +0100
Subject: Re: Outstanding invoice #INV-20261031 — VAT allocation and remit lock

Hi Hannah —

Thanks for the heads up and apologies for the delay. We're finalising internal entity mapping following a recent restructuring; that has held up the payment. Our controller is confirming which legal entity should be billed and whether the reverse-charge applies.

We expect to have a definitive answer by COB Monday (11/16). I have attached the bank rejection notice and a short note from our treasury team explaining the hold.

Please do not escalate to legal yet — we are committed to resolving this and will prioritise the payment once the entity is confirmed. If Redwood can accept a staged approach (release part of the balance while we clear the VAT paperwork) we can discuss amounts.

Regards,
Carlos
Head of Procurement, NovumHealth
[carlos@novumhealth.com]

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 13 Nov 2026 12:30:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Outstanding invoice #INV-20261031 — VAT allocation and remit lock

Team —

Thanks for the update. Quick assessment and recommended next actions from collections: 

- Classification: Priority A (key account, >30d, cross-border VAT question).
- Soft-dunning sequence to run: Day 1 (courtesy reminder — already sent), Day 4 (formal dunning with SLA for proof/payment), Day 10 (escalation to exec + potential service restrictions).
- Suggested staged-release offer: Redwood can accept 50% remit if Novum provides signed VAT declaration + payment instruction. This reduces our DSO risk while they finish entity mapping.

Legal/ops asks for Neha: please confirm whether a staged-release creates any compliance exposure (we need to ensure revenue recognition stays accurate across entities).

If we do not receive evidence by Monday COB (11/16), I recommend: 
1) Send formal dunning (templates ready).
2) Notify revenue ops to flag renewal holds and stop auto-billing.
3) Prep an exec summary to loop in VP Sales if no response by Day 10.

I can draft the Day 4 dunning email and the staged-release agreement if you want me to own execution.

—Kimberly
Kimberly Park
Manager, Collections & Credit
Redwood Inference

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 14 Nov 2026 16:02:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Outstanding invoice #INV-20261031 — VAT allocation and remit lock

Team —

Appreciate the context. Two quick decisions from finance: 
1) Approve the staged-release option at 50% conditional on receipt of a signed VAT declaration and cleared payment instruction. Collections, proceed to draft the agreement and send to Novum with a 72-hour turnaround.
2) If Novum fails to provide the necessary evidence/pay within the 72-hour window, escalate to exec (VP Sales + CFO) and issue the Day 10 service restriction notice.

Neha — please prepare a concise legal memo (1 page) outlining risks of staged-release and recommended contractual language for the release. Put it in the shared Drive folder and flag anything that requires VP approval.

Hannah — when you have Novum's payment stub or VAT doc, upload to the Drive link and mark the HubSpot deal D-2026-1193 as "pending remit-release". I will notify the CFO if we escalate.

Marcus
